metapropul A Practical Toolkit for Meta-Analysis in Systematic Reviews Welcome Welcome to metapropul A beginner-friendly R package for publication-ready meta-analysis — pooling evidence from proportions, ratios, and means with minimal code, maximal output. What is metapropul? metapropul is an R package designed for systematic reviewers who need to conduct and report meta-analyses without wrestling with low-level statistical plumbing. It wraps the battle-tested meta and metafor engines behind a clean, consistent interface guided by one simple philosophy: Beginners get everything with minimal code. Experts opt out rather than opt in. All sensible defaults are on. Customisation is available but never required. What can you do? 📊 Pool Effect Sizes Odds ratios, risk ratios, hazard ratios, mean differences, and proportions — all with one function call. 🌲 Forest Plots Publication-ready forest plots with automatic sizing, subgroup panels, and multiple layout styles. 🔍 Publication Bias Egger’s test, Begg’s test, trim-and-fill, contour-enhanced funnel plots, and limit meta-analysis. 📐 Heterogeneity I², τ², leave-one-out plots, and Baujat plots to understand between-study variation. 📉 Influence Analysis Leave-one-out diagnostics — forest plots and summary tables — to spot influential studies. 📋 Summary Tables gt-powered tables formatted for direct copy-paste into Word or PDF manuscripts. Quick start # Install from GitHub (CRAN submission pending) # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("drrubesh/metapropul") library(metapropul) # --- Proportions in 3 lines --- data(dat_bcg, package = "metapropul") result <- meta_prop(dat_bcg, event = "tpos", n = "npos", studylab = "author") forest_meta(result) How to use this book This documentation is organised as a guided tour: Chapter What you’ll learn Getting Started Installation, datasets, and your first analysis Ratio outcomes OR, RR, HR — binary event data Mean differences MD and SMD — continuous outcomes Proportions Single-arm proportions with PLOGIT / PFT Forest plots Customising and exporting forest plots Publication bias All tests and funnel plot variants Heterogeneity Diagnosing and visualising heterogeneity Influence analysis Leave-one-out diagnostics Meta-regression Exploring moderators Summary tables Manuscript-ready tables FAQ Common questions and troubleshooting About the author Rubeshkumar Polani is a systematic review methodologist and clinician with a passion for making evidence synthesis accessible to practitioners.
